context: Pick a scheme that survives '::' inside the command - a distinct separator, an escape, or accepting the structured --from JSON payload as the supported path for such rungs - and keep every existing 2-field and 3-field spec parsing exactly as it does now. Then repair the one mangled rung in the database, and add a lint finding for a stored command that does not lex, so the next occurrence is caught rather than discovered by hand.
description: _parse_verify_flag (todo_db.py) does fields = spec.split('::') with no maxsplit, then takes fields[0..2] as description, command, expected. pytest node IDs use the same '::' token, so the most natural targeted rung - a file plus class plus test - is shredded: everything after the first '::' inside the command moves into expected and the rest is dropped entirely. It is silent, with no error at create time and no lint finding afterwards, so the ladder looks well-formed while carrying a command that cannot run. Live victim on the tracker today: item test-export-invalid-output-dir-assumes-non-root seq 1 stored command 'uv run -- python -m pytest -n 0 (quote)tests/unit/cli/test_cli_output.py' with expected 'TestResultExporterErrorHandling(quote) -q' - truncated mid-quote, so it does not even lex. A shlex scan of every stored rung finds that one case of this defect; three other non-lexing rungs are prose written into the command field, a different problem. Note maxsplit alone does not fix it: with a 3-field spec the command still ends at its own first '::'. Needs a separator or escaping decision.

preserves.behavior: Existing specs of the form description plus command, and description plus command plus expected, parse exactly as they do today
